p.i: Forique solus arbiter boarij est: Forique solus arbiter piscarij est: Forique solus arbiter olitorij est: Forique solus arbiter cupedinis: Forumque cunctis publicum magis foris Res contrahentum consficit semper domi. Piscator, olitor, lanius, auceps, & coquus Illo absque nullum contrahunt commercium, Nec mula senio fracta, nec mulus tripes, Nec asinus ager, nec caballus morbidus Venum sine illo poterit ire interprete. Cuncta unde possit confici pecunia Vendit, reuendit, praestinat, habet quaestui. Nec vllus opifex, emtor est, aut venditor, Merx, ars, negotium, unde levis odor lucri Spirat, quod ille non sagax praesentiat, Non antevortat, occupétque & devoret. Aut si id negatur, portiunculam tamen Praerodat aliquam, solus & magnarius Mercator, idem solus & scrutarius. Si quis tot artes tractat unus sordidas, Hoc axe natus, gente nec Iudaeus est, Beleago dicam has tractat artes sordidas, Hoc axe natus, gente nec Iudaeus est.

main_text.head: IN EVNDEM.
main_text.p: BEleago cunctas nouit artes unice, Has praeter unas quas docet. Beleago cunctas tractat artes commodè, Has praeter unas, quas docet. Nec faenerator alter illo doctior, Nec caupo quisquam argutior,

page.notes: A handwritten word "Mango" in the lower right margin is an annotation, not printed text, and is left out. The initial B of the epigram is a large letter; it is joined to the following word. Some letters in the scan are faint, but the transcription follows the printed forms.
